questions.prompt: What is the procedure of an experiment?
questions.answer: A step-by-step list of how to do it
wrong: The final answer of the experiment
A guess about what will happen
questions.explain: A procedure lists every step so that someone else could repeat the experiment exactly.

questions.prompt: What is the independent variable in an experiment?
questions.answer: The factor you change on purpose
wrong: A factor that stays the same
questions.explain: The independent variable is the one thing the scientist chooses to change to see what happens.

questions.prompt: What is the dependent variable in an experiment?
questions.answer: The result you measure
wrong: The factor you change on purpose
questions.explain: The dependent variable "depends" on what you changed. It is the outcome you observe or measure.

questions.prompt: What are the constants in an experiment?
questions.answer: Factors kept the same in every trial
questions.explain: Keeping everything else the same makes it a fair test of the one thing you changed.

questions.prompt: What is the control in an experiment?
questions.answer: The trial used as a standard for comparison
wrong: The scientist in charge of the lab
The variable that changes the most
The graph of the final results
questions.explain: The control is left unchanged so you can compare it with the trials where you did change something.

questions.prompt: What is the best way to record data while an experiment is happening?
questions.answer: In a data table
questions.explain: Tables in rows and columns are quick to fill in and easy to compare. Graphs can be made later.

questions.prompt: What do engineers mainly do?
questions.answer: Design and build things that solve problems
questions.explain: Engineers invent and improve machines, structures and products to meet real-world needs.

questions.prompt: What is a prototype?
questions.answer: An early model of a design that can be tested
wrong: The finished product sold in stores
A list of the design's limits
questions.explain: A prototype is like a first draft. Engineers test it, then adjust it to make it better.

questions.prompt: You play music to some plants and not to others, then measure how tall they grow. What is the independent variable?
questions.answer: Whether the plant hears music
questions.explain: Music is what you chose to change on purpose, so it is the independent variable.

questions.prompt: You play music to some plants and not to others, then measure how tall they grow. What is the dependent variable?
questions.answer: How tall the plants grow
questions.explain: Plant height is the result you measure, and it may depend on the music.

questions.prompt: On a line graph, where does the independent variable usually go?
questions.answer: On the x-axis (horizontal)
questions.explain: The independent variable goes along the bottom (x-axis), and the dependent variable goes up the side (y-axis).

questions.prompt: Which graph is best for comparing how many students have each kind of pet?
questions.answer: A bar graph
questions.explain: Bar graphs compare amounts in separate categories, like dogs, cats and birds.

questions.prompt: Which graph best shows a plant growing taller week by week?
questions.answer: A line graph
questions.explain: Line graphs are great for showing steady change over time.

questions.prompt: What is a circle graph (pie chart) best for showing?
questions.answer: How parts make up a whole
wrong: The exact path of a moving car
questions.explain: Each slice of a circle graph is a share of the total, like how a class splits its votes.

questions.prompt: What does it mean to infer?
questions.answer: Use evidence to reach a conclusion you didn't see
wrong: Guess with no evidence at all
questions.explain: When you can't watch something happen, you can use clues and facts to figure out what likely happened.

questions.prompt: Why should you run several trials of an experiment?
questions.answer: To make sure the results are reliable
wrong: To change the hypothesis each time
So the results come out different
questions.explain: Small errors happen. If many trials give similar results, you can trust them more.

questions.prompt: You test whether adding more salt to water makes an egg float. What should you keep constant?
questions.answer: The size of the egg and the amount of water
questions.explain: Salt is what you change, and floating is what you measure. Everything else should stay the same.

questions.prompt: Why should you change only one variable at a time in an experiment?
questions.answer: So you know what caused the result
wrong: So the graph has more colors
questions.explain: If you change two things at once, you can't tell which one made the difference.

questions.prompt: What does a scatter plot help you see?
questions.answer: Whether two sets of data are related
questions.explain: Each dot is a pair of numbers. The pattern of dots shows whether one goes up or down with the other.

questions.prompt: On a scatter plot, what do you call a point that is far away from the general pattern?
questions.answer: An outlier
questions.explain: An outlier doesn't follow the trend of the other points.

questions.prompt: What does a line of best fit show on a scatter plot?
questions.answer: The overall trend of the data points
wrong: The exact value of every point
questions.explain: The line of best fit sums up how the points are related, even if few points sit right on it.

questions.prompt: Which numbers make a good scale for a graph axis?
questions.explain: A scale should go up in even steps so the graph isn't stretched or squished in places.

questions.prompt: In engineering, what are constraints?
questions.answer: Limits such as cost, time or materials
wrong: The final drawing of the design
questions.explain: Constraints are restrictions that a design must work within, like a small budget.

questions.prompt: An engineer's prototype fails its test. What usually happens next?
questions.answer: Improve the design and test it again
wrong: Sell it to the public anyway
Stop working on the problem forever
questions.explain: Engineers learn from what didn't work, redesign, and test again until it solves the problem.
